newsitem.title: HUNGARY: Hungary sees no '97 sugar export after '96 failure.
newsitem.headline: Hungary sees no '97 sugar export after '96 failure.

text.p: Hungary will not export sugar in 1997 after loss-making exports in 1996, Andras Angeli, chairman of the Sugar Industry Association (SIA), said on Friday.
"Last year we had signs of a 600,000 tonne sugar beet demand from Croatia, Slovenia and Serbia...but we could only export 200,000 tonnes," Angeli told Reuters.
"The rest was processed in Hungary and we exported some of the (excess) sugar at a loss due to depressed world market prices."
He said this year the planted area was down to 96,471 hectares from last year's 110,742 and the crop would probably be 3.8 to four million tonnes, compared with 4.6 million last year.
That would translate into 456,000 tonnes of sugar, enough to cover domestic demand. "Domestic demand has been between 420,000 and 450,000 tonnes per year over the last three years," Angeli said.
He added that the root to leaf ratio of Hungary's beet was much healthier this year than in previous years, when July and August proved very dry.
The average leaf weight per root was 619 grams on samples taken on August 11 for the second test released earlier on Friday, compared with 522 grams last year, SIA figures showed.
"The foliage is strong and if we have appropriate weather in September, we would have a very good year," Angeli said.
